chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Signing with Verne Records and the Rapping Day name
summary: Cuevas's Verne label recorded Miguelito, Guerra, Trio San Juan and Machito; Guerra's Rapping Day was a pseudonym.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay then, we'll get around to that. In 1945, you signed a contract with Verne records.
Do you remember how that came about?

Well, Miguelito Valdes was free-lancing so this company, Verne, owned by Cuevas, he approached us. Miguelito, Marcelino Guerra, Trio San Juan, myself,/and he wanted to make a 'catalog so that particular time we recorded with and a few other bands
Okay, I notice from the catalog that I have that they have an orchestra called Rapping Day.

That's Marcelino Guerra. Now, some of the recordings with Rapping Day, you are on them. Now, whose orchestra was that? Was that you singing with Marcelino, duets with his orchestra or was Marcelino singing with your orchestra?
I dan't recall very well, but I think it was his orchestra.
He named that band, Rapping Day because he was signed with another company and he want to.....

I see, I see. Ahh, yes I got it mixed-up now. He was using the name Marcelino Guerra, for Verne and he was recording for Coda on that Rapping Day. Okay, I got it now. All right, they were ahh - no, Marcelino Guerra Orchestra and then your name is on that, right? Also Verne has recordings of Miguelito Valdes singing duets with Machito.
